subject: Request: temporary log stewardship and erase-exception for Radcliffe integration
messages:
From: Joe Turner <joe.turner@radcliffehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@radcliffehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: temporary log stewardship for Radcliffe integrations

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from our side — we have an ongoing patient-data reconciliation and a short audit window tied to a regulatory review. The audit team needs a 60-day snapshot of request+session logs for a single Radcliffe tenant (tenant id: RDX-921) that would otherwise be pruned by your standard 30-day rolling TTL.

Can Redwood temporarily preserve the full request/session logs for this tenant for 60 days (start 2026-11-07) rather than your default retention? Our security folks will need SOC 2 report extracts and any relevant SIG/CAIQ mappings that speak to log handling and deletion mechanics. Legal also asked for a one-off amendment or letter confirming the preservation window and the deletion plan afterwards.

We can provide a PO if needed and will sign any reasonable amendment. I attached a short incident timeline for context.

Thanks,
Joe Turner
Director, Infrastructure & Security
Radcliffe Health

Attachment: incident-timeline.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Joe Turner <joe.turner@radcliffehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log stewardship for Radcliffe integrations

Joe — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Appreciate the incident timeline; that helps.

Short answer: we can accommodate a customer-specific preservation window, but we need to coordinate security, legal, and the operations windowing to ensure it meets our SOC 2 controls and doesn’t create cross-tenant exposure.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal confirmation of feasibility (ops/security) — Ben/Marissa, can you weigh in on feasibility and any guardrails (segmented export vs. extended TTL, encryption-at-rest constraints, and how we will guarantee deletion at the end date)?
- I'll share SOC 2 summary extracts and the CAIQ/SIG crosswalk as requested once we confirm approach.
- If legal signs the amendment, we'll accept a 60-day retention window limited to tenant RDX-921, with a targeted deletion run on 2027-01-06 and audit evidence delivered after deletion.

We should also confirm whether Radcliffe prefers an in-place preservation (extend TTL for that tenant only) or an export+escrow approach (we retain a sealed export in our secure store and perform deletion from the live system). Each has tradeoffs for retrieval and proof of deletion.

Joe — can you confirm which approach you prefer, or should we propose both with pros/cons?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

---
On Thu, 5 Nov 2026 at 09:12, Joe Turner <joe.turner@radcliffehealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Jordan,
>
> Quick note from our side — we have an ongoing patient-data reconciliation...
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:31:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Request: temporary log stewardship for Radcliffe integrations

Jordan — tagging in ops/security perspective. TL;DR: feasible with controls and legal amendment. Details below.

Feasibility notes:
- We can implement a tenant-scoped TTL override for RDX-921 to 60 days. This is the least disruptive and fastest route.
- Alternate: export-to-escrow (encrypted S3) — we can create a sealed export and mark the live tenant for normal TTL; export stored with customer-specific KMS wrapping for the 60-day window. This gives stronger forensic separation but requires export/ingest runbooks.

Controls required:
- Limit access: only a specific ops role and an approved security reviewer will have access to the preserved logs.
- Audit trail: we'll capture deletion run logs and provide a signed deletion certificate after the retention window ends.
- Evidence package: SOC 2 report extract (logs/retention control section), CAIQ sheet rows mapping to log handling, and a config snapshot showing tenant-level TTL override.

Legal/Commercial ask: we need a signed minimal amendment — 1 paragraph defining tenant RDX-921, preservation window (2026-11-07 to 2027-01-06), confirmation of deletion procedure, and liability language. Marissa, can you draft?

Impact to pricing: small one-time admin fee for export-to-escrow; TTL override has no additional charge in our standard enterprise terms (recommend TTL override unless Radcliffe specifically wants escrow).

Attachments: radcliffe-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Joe Turner <joe.turner@radcliffehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: temporary log stewardship for Radcliffe integrations

Joe — following up with the plan and next steps. Thanks for the patience while we confirmed internally.

Summary of what Redwood will do for tenant RDX-921:
1) Approach: perform a tenant-scoped TTL override to preserve request/session logs for 60 days (2026-11-07 through 2027-01-06).
2) Access & controls: access limited to named ops role and security reviewer; logs remain encrypted at rest; we will capture an immutable audit trail for any access during the window.
3) Evidence: we will provide the following deliverables 7 business days after deletion (on or before 2027-01-13):
   - Signed deletion certificate (PDF) with timestamps and checksum summary.
   - SOC 2 report extract (redacted as required).
   - CAIQ/SIG mapping rows relevant to log handling and deletion mechanics.
   - Config snapshot showing the TTL override and the deletion job output.
4) Legal: attached is a one-paragraph amendment that your counsel can sign (see attached draft). If Radcliffe prefers export-to-escrow instead, there's a small admin fee — let us know.

Please reply with a quick confirmation ("approve TTL override" or "request export-escrow") and we'll put the amendment and the change control in motion. Once we have the signed amendment and confirmation to proceed we will schedule the change for 2026-11-07.

DocuSign and the amendment draft are available here: https://www.docusign.com/transaction/EXAMPLE-12345
Google Drive with the evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleRadcliffeEvidence

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: radcliffe-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 18 KB)
